Variants.Content: Acorn Hall is the traditional seat of House Smallwood in the Riverlands, located where the Red Fork River meets the woodlands. Oak trees and rivers together provide the local area with timber, grazing, hunting and farming land, but they also keep the territory in an easily traversable zone. The nobles of the Riverlands could rarely sleep with just one castle: there were too many roads, too many rivers, and the neighbors were too close; an army could burn mills, seize cattle, and cut off ferries without attacking a city. Family life in Acorn Hall thus always oscillates between the etiquette of the hall and the reality of the field.

Entry Acorn Hall Local families also relied on river transportation, ferries, wheat fields, mills, and hiding places when war came; if any road, well, spring, or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Acorn Hall If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

The craftsmen use their hands to measure the stone walls, wooden beams, iron doors, tombs and seams left by generations of repairs in the Acorn Hall. The priests use rituals to continue the memory of the seven gods, the legend of the ancient river king and the land that has changed hands repeatedly. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Acorn Hall They care about river transportation, ferries, wheat fields, mills, and hiding places when war comes. They also care about whether seeds are left after collecting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
